sections.title: 1. Free
sections.body: Free costs nothing. You get 3 templates and 1 PDF. There is nothing to refund.

sections.title: 2. One-time purchases
sections.body: Paid options are one-time. You can buy nicer templates, smart writing credits, or both. There is no monthly subscription and nothing renews automatically. Payments are processed via KHQR or Card.

sections.title: 3. When we refund
list: Within 7 days of a purchase, you can request a full refund if you have not used the credits and have not unlocked or downloaded a paid template PDF
Accidental duplicate charges are refunded in full

sections.title: 4. When we do not refund
list: Credits, job analyses, or interview sets you have already used
A paid template you have already unlocked, or a paid PDF you have already downloaded
Requests made more than 7 days after the charge, except for duplicate charges

sections.title: 5. How to request a refund
sections.body: Contact us with your account email and the date of the charge. See the Contact page. We aim to respond within 2 business days and send approved refunds to your original payment method (KHQR or Card) within 5 to 10 business days.

sections.title: 1. Information we collect
sections.body: We collect the information you give us directly: your name, email, phone number, and the content of any resume you build with Resumate (work history, education, skills, and similar details).
list: Account info you provide when you sign in with Google
Resume content you type or paste, including job advertisements you analyze
Usage data such as pages visited, features used, and purchases, to improve the product

sections.title: 2. How we use your information
sections.body: We use your information to build and store your resumes, run smart features you choose to use (job analysis, match scoring, interview questions, readiness reports), process one-time payments, and improve Resumate. We do not sell your personal data to third parties.

sections.title: 3. Smart processing
sections.body: If you use smart writing, job analysis, or interview prep, resume content and pasted job advertisements may be sent to our smart providers to generate suggestions, scores, and questions. This content is used only to serve your request and is not used to train shared models without your consent.

sections.title: 4. Data sharing
sections.body: We share data only with service providers who help us run Resumate, such as payment processors (Card, Bakong/KHQR) and cloud hosting, under confidentiality obligations. We may disclose information if required by law.

sections.title: 5. Data retention & control
sections.body: You can edit or delete your resumes and account at any time from Settings. Deleting your account removes your personal data and stored resumes within 30 days, except where retention is required by law.

sections.title: 6. Your rights
sections.body: You may request a copy of your data, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it by contacting us; see the Contact page.

sections.title: 7. Contact us
sections.body: Questions about this policy? Reach us at privacy@Resumate.app or visit our Contact page.

sections.title: 1. Acceptance of terms
sections.body: By creating an account or using Resumate, you agree to these Terms of Service and our Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, please do not use the platform.

sections.title: 2. Your account
list: You sign in with Google; you are responsible for keeping that account secure
You must be at least 16 years old to use Resumate
One account per person; accounts created to abuse free templates may be suspended

sections.title: 3. Payments
sections.body: Paid features are one-time purchases, not subscriptions. They do not renew. Payments are processed via KHQR or Card. See our Refund Policy for refund terms.
list: You can pay once for templates, smart writing credits, or both
Unlocked templates stay on your account. Unused credits stay until you use them. Used credits are not restored except as described in the Refund Policy

sections.title: 4. Your content & acceptable use
list: You own the resumes and other content you create; we only use it to provide and improve the service
Smart suggestions are provided as a starting point; you are responsible for reviewing accuracy before use
Do not upload unlawful, infringing, or abusive content, or attempt to disrupt, reverse-engineer, or scrape the platform

sections.title: 5. Service availability & disclaimer
sections.body: Resumate is provided "as is." We work to keep the platform reliable but do not guarantee uninterrupted access, and we are not liable for job outcomes, interview results, or decisions made by employers.

sections.title: 6. Changes & contact
sections.body: We may update these terms from time to time; continued use after a change means you accept the update. Questions? Reach out on the Contact page.

hero.title: Built in Cambodia,
hero.subtitle: Resumate started with a simple frustration: too many talented students were paying strangers on Facebook just to get a resume that they couldn't even edit afterward.

story.label: Why we started
story.title: The $2.99 problem nobody
story.p1: Every year, thousands of students graduate from universities across Cambodia ready to start their careers. But there is a quiet barrier between them and their first job application: the resume.
story.p2: Without an affordable, locally built tool, most job seekers turn to informal resume writers on Facebook and Telegram paying two to six dollars each time, waiting days for a draft, and ending up with a file they cannot edit themselves when something needs to change.
story.quote: "We didn't want to build another resume tool. We wanted to build the tool we wished existed when we were applying for our first jobs."
story.p3: That's why Resumate exists. Start free with a real resume you can edit and download. If you want nicer templates or smart writing help, you pay once. No monthly bill. And it goes further than the PDF: job match, skill gaps, and interview prep when you're ready.

mission.label: Our mission
mission.title: Make a great resume accessible to every
mission.subtitle: We believe where you went to university or how confident your English is shouldn't decide whether you get a fair shot at a job interview.

cards.title: Pay for what you need
cards.desc: Templates, smart writing, or both. One-time prices a Cambodian student can actually afford, not a monthly US software bill.

cards.title: Built for two languages
cards.desc: Read every instruction in Khmer or English, while your resume content stays in English exactly what employers expect.

cards.title: Beyond the resume
cards.desc: Most platforms stop once the resume is done. Resumate continues analyzing job ads, matching your skills, and preparing you for the interview.

items.title: Your data stays yours

tips.lead: Header & Contact Details Your first impression on employers.
points: Use the full English name you intend to use on official job applications.
Specify your target job role (e.g., Junior Accountant or Marketing Assistant) rather than 'Student'.
Provide an active email address and phone number that you monitor daily.
Include a 2 to 3 sentence summary highlighting your academic background, key strength, and career objective no extensive work history required.

tips.lead: Work & Practical Experience Showcasing your career story.
points: List roles in reverse chronological order (most recent first).
Include job title, company, location, and dates.
Start each bullet with a strong action verb (e.g. Built, Organized, Coordinated).
Quantify results where you can (e.g. Collaborated with 3 teammates, Served 20+ clients daily).
Keep 3 to 5 bullets per role focused on impact, not daily duties.

tips.lead: Education & Honors Highlighting your academic background.
points: List your most recent educational institution first.
State the full degree name and university title.
Include your GPA if it is 3.5 or higher, or if you graduated with honors.
Under 'Achievements', highlight scholarship awards, Dean’s List honors, or relevant coursework.

tips.lead: Skills & Languages Demonstrating your core capabilities.
points: List 6 to 10 tools or technologies you are proficient in (e.g., Excel, Figma, Python).
Prioritize accuracy over length be realistic about your proficiency level.
Include language proficiencies (e.g., Khmer, English), as bilingual ability is highly valued in Cambodia.
References are optional; you may omit them or state 'Available upon request'.

tips.lead: Review & Export Final quality checks before applying.
points: Review your optimization score and address any outstanding checklist items.
Proofread the live preview carefully to eliminate spelling or grammatical errors.
Keep your resume to a clean, well-formatted single page.
Export as a PDF formatted as 'FirstName_LastName_Resume.pdf'.

tipHasExperience.lead: Work & Practical Experience Showcasing your career story.
points: List roles in reverse chronological order (most recent first).
Include job title, company, location, and dates.
Start each bullet with a strong action verb (e.g. Built, Organized, Coordinated).
Quantify results where you can (e.g. Collaborated with 3 teammates, Served 20+ clients daily).
Keep 3 to 5 bullets per role focused on impact, not daily duties.
Need an internship or project too? Tap Add experience and pick that type.

tipFreshExperience.lead: No formal job yet internships, projects, volunteering, and part-time work still count.
points: Tap Add experience and pick Internship, School project, Volunteer, or Part-time.
Write what you did, who you helped, and one small result if you have it.
Even “supported a 5-person team” is useful.
List the most recent activity first.
Start each description with an action verb (e.g. Built, Organized, Coordinated).

tipExperienceChoice.lead: Jobs, internships, and school projects all belong on this page.
points: Tap Add experience and pick the type that matches what you did.
A company job, an internship, and a school project can sit in the same list.
Start with the most recent.
Write what you did, and one result if you have it.
